decisions.reason: As a niche but low-cost digital engineering tool tied to the firm's solution business, it is likely kept unless usage and lead-generation outcomes remain clearly below aspiration levels.

After withdrawing the related Product A, management would usually retain the stronger fouling-detection offering because it fits the established portfolio and can absorb related know-how and resources.

This newly launched weir product is close to the firm's core water-control business, so an expanding firm with some slack would normally give it more time unless early sales disappoint relative to comparable products.

The energy management system matches the firm's strategic direction toward digitally networked, efficient infrastructure, making it likely to be supported even if early market feedback is still forming.

A multi-model overflow flap gate line with its own presentation page is a strong sign of commitment in a core application area, so management would likely continue it unless results fall well short of aspirations.
